title: Enforce public-safe boundaries in blog source and rendered output
goal: Add deterministic, repository-owned checks that reject high-confidence local-path, private-source, and credential-shaped material before blog content can pass the existing source and rendered-site validation layers.
non_goals: Replace human privacy or editorial review
Read the private knowledge graph or any private source repository
Publish content or merge pull requests automatically
invariants: Failure output identifies the file, line, and rule but never echoes the matched secret or private value
Only high-confidence patterns are enforced to avoid blocking ordinary technical prose
Draft source content is checked before it can later become publishable
Existing Hugo, metadata, content, rendered-post, RSS, crawl, distribution, brand, domain, and photo checks remain authoritative
acceptance_criteria: A shared detector recognizes file URIs, absolute user-home paths on macOS/Linux/Windows, the private-source marker llm-wiki-ranjib:, and credential-shaped GitHub, OpenAI, and AWS tokens
Detector regression probes include rejected examples and safe near-misses, and failure reports do not contain the matched material
The source content-model validator checks every Markdown post, including drafts, with the shared detector
The rendered-post validator checks generated post HTML with the shared detector
The full repository build, lint, and test validator routes pass on the current public corpus
No automatic publication or merge is introduced
security_constraints: Do not inspect or copy any private knowledge-graph content
Do not print matched credentials or private paths in validation output
Do not add network access or third-party dependencies
Do not weaken existing public-source, approved-photo, brand, or domain controls
uncertainties: The initial high-confidence pattern set may need reviewed expansion as new export formats appear
A deterministic leak check reduces accidental exposure but cannot establish that prose is contextually safe to publish
